A mechanized unit driven berserk by Devour contamination, capable of annihilating enemies with overwhelming firepower. Valente was sharp, efficient, and relentlessly ambitious, maintaining absolute focus on his work while constantly striving for bigger things. In recognition of his exceptional contributions, the company digitized his consciousness so he could continue serving the corporation and inspire future generations of employees.
A Devourborne parasitized by shards of a Disturbance Core — once a person who staggered through the darkness of the night.

An apex predator within its ecosystem, transformed into a terrifying beast after being infected by Devour Energy. Massive in size and immensely destructive, it possesses an extreme territorial instinct and violently attacks all intruders. Observations suggest it retains traces of social behavior, including violently dominating others of its kind into submission.
[Note: It dislikes the smell of bird droppings. Smearing some on yourself may help avoid its horrifying attacks.]

A Devourborne formed from the fusion of a giant sheathbeetle and a radio pulse transmitter. It lurks deep underground, forbidding anyone from approaching the forbidden secrets buried there. The creature's head is a military-grade radio pulse transmitter once used to guide intercontinental strategic weapons with pinpoint accuracy. Now, it serves only one purpose: to stand watch and annihilate anyone reckless enough to uncover the ugly truth.

A humanoid robot whose logic circuits were disrupted by Devour. Originally designed with the protection of personnel in mind, the robot's blades have now become the very shadow feared by those it was meant to protect.

A riot-control robot whose logic circuits were disrupted by Devour. Armed with a vector rifle, it delivers precise and lethal shots with ruthless efficiency. People always loved machines this efficient, right up until that efficiency was turned against them.

A labor robot whose logic circuits malfunctioned under the effects of Devour. The chainsaw it carries was originally meant to clear obstacles and carve out paths to safety. Who would've thought it could carve through people just as easily?

A riot-control robot whose logic circuits malfunctioned under the effects of Devour. It used to be deployed against employees dissatisfied with company policy, and now everyone gets a turn under its steel baton.
A riot-control robot whose logic circuits malfunctioned under the effects of Devour. It can detach part of its own power core and launch it as an explosive attack.

A security robot whose logic circuits malfunctioned under the effects of Devour. Designed specifically to protect high-value personnel, this premium model was equipped with advanced martial arts and close-combat techniques, making it the top choice among corporate clients. The company's customer support lines are probably overwhelmed by now.

A heavily armored corporate operative. Due to the direct integration between its nervous system and mechanical linkages, Devour has driven it into a state of madness, causing it to attack anything that approaches. A premium product custom-made for elite corporate clients. Human trafficking, you say? No, we prefer to call it "lifetime employment."

A war machine buried deep within a research facility, now uncontrollably activated by Devour. Any who approach are obliterated by its overwhelming firepower. A monster forged from the company's obsession and an impossible ambition, intended to symbolize the dawn of a new era. They named it "Adam." But in the end, it was nothing more than a childish and greedy fantasy. Just like this machine itself, it lacked a true "foundation."

A hybrid Devourborne formed from a video display unit and a spider. A relatively rare type of Devourborne commonly found in human settlements consumed by Devour. Rumor has it these Screenspider Husks project terrifying visions tailored to their victims' deepest fears, luring them step by step into deadly traps before hunting them down...
[Note: The rumor is false, but its playback content can be influenced via close-range signal transmission. However, the result is usually a snow-like pattern of scrambled interference.]

A Devourborne fused from a giant python and a sonic energy amplifier. Under the influence of Devour Energy, the two merged together, with clear signs of crude surgical stitching still visible. The Serpent Husk can unleash multiple forms of Devour radiation through the acoustic arrays in its head, requiring extreme caution when engaging it. It can also slam into enemies with terrifying leaps. Judging from the bloodstains splattered across its body, the mad scientists who pursued their twisted obsession likely paid the same brutal price themselves. A grim thought...

A Devourborne fused from a large beast and an information frequency modulator. Under the influence of Devour Energy, the two merged together, with clear signs of crude surgical stitching still visible. Frequency Beasthusks rarely take the initiative to attack, but they can broadcast signals that summon various Devoured Remains to fight alongside them. Whether this mutation was guided by the destructive will of Devour, or was the creature's original intended purpose, has long since been buried beneath ice and snow.

A hybrid Devourborne created from a receiver fused with a massive beast. Despite its enormous body, it attacks with shocking speed and crushing force far beyond normal understanding. Even enhanced by Devour Energy, biological and mechanical lifeforms should not be able to integrate this perfectly. Yet from the mechanical chips embedded deep in the bone and the sutured seams along the edges of the body, one can glimpse fragments of a terrible truth from the past...

After an unknown world was destroyed by Primordial Devour, what remained were echoes of the beings that once lived there, left behind within the Devour itself. They possess no thought or intelligence, only a fierce, unending aggression formed from the will of that world's final collapse, driving them to slaughter one another without end.

A lone knight wandering through the twilight of Primordial Devour. Though merely a lingering shadow cast into the Devour from some forgotten era, he carved his way through countless lost echoes and emerged with overwhelming strength and unshakable battle instinct. Even now, he maintains a stance perfectly suited for combat at all times. Even the mighty apostles avoid crossing blades with him lightly. A warrior of such caliber could never have been a nobody in his own age.
A massive fan wheel still churns the factory's energy systems, continuing to run even though the facility has long been abandoned.
Silent and hollow, this place is steeped in a strange blend of allure, illusion, and death.
After the final thrust of the Ground Basic Attack combo, times the input to perform a turning counter-thrust.

Humans are drawn to dreams, longing for boundless beauty, for an end to sorrow. Yet they also face reality and move toward the future. That is the resolve and courage we are meant to have.
Bring closure to a past that has already faded away.
The power plant has been affected by Devour, and the military robots inside have gone rogue. You are to proceed to the target location immediately and eliminate the threat.
A control sector that manages the entire factory's data systems, storing a large volume of classified information.
The main factory hall connected to the elevator shafts. It was once built by fearless people who laid the foundations of both the facility and Orum City itself.
A maintenance workshop where precision assembly lines reflect the facility's former glory.
From classified industrial test data to the idle complaints of workers, countless streams of information once flowed and were stored here.
It was nothing more than the delusion of an ambitious individual, yet paid for with the lives of countless innocents.
Due to the activity of mutated organisms, maintenance nodes like these are scattered across the outskirts and underground areas of Orum City. Any damage to them signals an impending crisis.

Any mutated creature approaching will trigger an alert. Unlike maintenance nodes, these function more like alarm beacons, distributed around suburban and residential zones of Orum City to provide early warning against various threats.
These underground tunnels were built for Orum City's future development. Though construction stopped long ago, they still embody the peak of the city's era of ambition and its vision of the future.
Once used for wastewater processing in Orum City, this area is now filled with all kinds of strange creatures. With the march of time, it was abandoned along with the underground infrastructure.
A collapsed passage, buried deep underground alongside the rest of the subterranean infrastructure in the wake of that catastrophe.
You recovered the final data cache, but the anomalies you'd encountered along the way made you decide to press onward.
LIAN channels her Special Abilities to summon countless blades, devastating all enemies within range and entering <color=#0b77c7>Manifestation</color> state.

After diving headfirst into high-society gossip, you learned that Mr. Will had been keeping the dog to curry favor with an influential figure at City Hall, which explained the excessive fuss. Two socialites also provided a lead: the missing orb might have ended up inside a Devouring Area.
TACO received another report. Coincidentally, a miner working in the Devouring Area had also lost a toy ball matching the description of Mr. Will's missing one.
The miner admitted he had found the toy ball and intended to keep it for himself, only to lose it afterward.
The miner confirmed this was the ball he had lost — well, technically the one he had picked up. So much for turning in lost property.
You handed the "valuable" toy ball over to TACO, hoping the Black Hall wouldn't have to deal with another ridiculous case like this anytime soon.

The dog went missing again, and this time it no longer recognized the toy ball in Mr. Will's hand. It only responded to the most expensive one instead. In the end, Mr. Will bought the priciest ball available and once again reclaimed his status as the dog's owner.

On a whim, I activated the mechanical cat, hoping it could help me find something suitable to keep as a pet.
After surviving a fierce battle, I began to suspect that the true objective of this journey might itself have been a Devourborne. But by then, there was no choice left except to keep moving forward.
The mechanical cat stopped in a corner and what it found was a strange little bug. Could that really count as a pet?

I came across a couple arguing over a gift. One of them, desperate to win back his heartbroken partner, hired me to help find a suitable pet. And the assistant he provided me with was... a bizarre mechanical cat.
While making my way forward, I ran into a staff member hiding nearby. According to her, some terrifying creature was waiting further ahead.
I reunited with the couple while carrying that so-called "pet" with me. Hopefully they weren't too shocked by what they were about to see.
To my surprise, they seemed absolutely thrilled with the "pet" I brought them. Carrying the little creature with them, the couple happily ran off toward their future together...

Before the eyes ever open, it's easiest to slip from one dream into another, struggling and sinking through desires buried deep within the heart, until the net woven by your will pulls you back to reality...

You received an invitation from ROCHE, who wanted to have dinner with you at the Crab House.

While dining with ROCHE at the Crab House, you noticed the food quality had dropped significantly. After speaking with the owner, you learned he had been experimenting with new recipes. You and ROCHE decided to help him develop the dishes and gather the ingredients he needed.
A Keystone employee happened to have the ingredients you needed, but in exchange, you had to help recover some lost cargo.
You returned the lost cargo to the Keystone employee and received the ingredient you needed in return.
After gathering all the ingredients, the owner thanked you sincerely and promised to give you special discounts in the future.

You came across a Keystone employee arguing with a coworker. After asking around, you learned they were desperately trying to recruit a new member into an organization called "More In, More Out." Hoping to investigate the group, you decided to attend one of their recruitment seminars.

You met the person in charge of the "More In, More Out" Foundation. After listening to the presentation, the Keystone employee became even more determined to join, only for the organizer to demand additional fees under various excuses.
After paying the extra fee, the organizer came up with yet another excuse to demand even more money.

After collecting the additional payment, the organizer tried to make an excuse and leave, only to be stopped and arrested by the Black Hall personnel on the spot. The farce finally came to an end, and the scammed Keystone employee was forced to face reality.

You decided not to pay any more fees and contacted the Black Hall instead. However, your actions alerted the organizer, who quickly fled the scene. Even so, the Keystone employee was finally able to accept that he had been scammed.

You encountered a visibly anxious staff member searching for her three missing coworkers. Apparently, she had something extremely important to discuss with them. You agreed to help track them down and bring them back to the base.
You came across a staff member collecting rocks. Hoping to help her return to camp sooner, you decided to gather the stones she needed on her behalf.
You handed over the rocks you collected to the staff member obsessed with rock collecting, and she happily returned to the base.
You encountered a staff member busy marking Devourborne in the area. To speed up her work, you decided to clear out the nearby Devourborne yourself.
After eliminating the nearby Devourborne, you helped the staff member finish her task, and she returned to the base satisfied.
You encountered a staff member slacking off. With her break interrupted, she reluctantly headed back to the base.

All of the staff eventually returned to the base, though the atmosphere among them remained tense. At a critical moment, your well-timed words helped everyone open up. Once they finally spoke honestly about their feelings, the argument at last came to an end.
You managed to locate all of the missing staff members and prepared to head back to the base.

You encountered someone claiming to be a "Devourborne linguist," who insisted on having discovered a Devourborne capable of speaking and asking you to go deeper into the cave in search of this miraculous creature together.
It seemed you were getting very close to the so-called talking Devourborne.

Deep within the cave, you encountered another scholar making strange noises in a self-invented "Devourborne language." That turned out to be the truth behind the "talking Devourborne," and the self-proclaimed linguist was utterly devastated upon learning the truth.

You encountered an employee muttering to herself and learned from her that another staff member had recently been acting strangely before suddenly leaving the base for unknown reasons. Concerned for her safety, you decided to go look for her.
You encountered the oddly behaving employee and discovered that she was attempting to become a Devivor through some extremely questionable methods.

You followed the strange employee and found her trying to awaken Devivor powers by carrying cargo far beyond her physical limits before eventually collapsing from the strain. You decided to help her change her ways...
After she woke up, you told her the truth. Though briefly discouraged, she soon pulled herself together and headed off to her next "training site."
After she woke up, you lied and told her she showed signs of awakening Devivor powers. Thrilled by the news, she eagerly rushed off to her next "training site."

You followed the strange employee and discovered that she was attempting to awaken Devivor powers by confronting Devourborne head-on. She soon fainted from sheer terror. You decided to clear out the Devourborne for her.
After dealing with the Devourborne, you decided to help her change her ways...
After she woke up, you told her the truth. Though briefly discouraged, she ultimately decided to return to the base.
After she woke up, you lied and told her she showed signs of awakening Devivor powers. After an excited outburst, she decided to return to the base.

The aspiring Devivor returned to the base, but under your influence, she became extremely arrogant and firmly convinced that she had truly become a Devivor. Whether that was a good thing or not... you couldn't really say.

The aspiring Devivor returned to the base, but under your influence, she became even stranger and started experimenting with even more bizarre methods to become a Devivor. Whether that was a good thing or not... you couldn't really say.

The aspiring Devivor returned to the base, but under your influence, she became deeply insecure and accepted her fate as an ordinary person. Whether that was a good thing or not... you couldn't really say.

You came across two groups of civilians arguing over the nature of Devour. The disagreement stemmed from how little each side truly knew about the world beyond the bastion. To settle the dispute, you decided to head outside and take photographs showing the real conditions out there.
You encountered several Devourborne. Before taking any photos, it was probably best to take them out first.
You took photos of the Devourborne. A stray kitten wandered into the shots, though that probably wasn't a big deal.

You took photos of a Devouring Rift. A stray kitten wandered into the shots, though that probably wasn't a big deal.

You brought the photos back to the arguing crowd, but everyone still interpreted the situation differently, and the argument continued. However, once someone noticed the kitten in the photos, the entire discussion shifted toward the cat instead. Losing interest in arguing about Devour, the crowd eventually dispersed.

"The test results have already confirmed that this vine staff was not a stage prop crafted by human hands. Both the wooden structure and the gem-like inlays are composed of entirely unknown materials. It originated from a spacetime completely unlike our own. From this, we may reasonably speculate that somewhere in the universe, there truly existed a civilization that relied on staffs to wield magic. Their aptitude for manipulating magic appears strikingly similar to humanity's Tenebrium resistance seen in Attuners. What is obvious, however, is that this staff has been completely corrupted by Tenebrium. Could this, in some way, signify the downfall of that civilization? And if even magic ultimately failed to save them... then what fate awaits us in the world of Halo?"
—Live Commentator Luscinia Christina, excerpt from Century New Knowledge, Issue 312

This discovery was unlike anything we'd encountered before. This unassuming glass tube may point to an astonishing possibility—that the lifeforms within this Spatiotemporal Fragment were actually breeding Devourborne the same way we raise livestock. I once attempted similar research myself, but every experiment ended in failure. Devourborne don't just bring Tenebrium and danger—they also tend to attack with complete disregard for their own survival. Under laboratory conditions, expecting them to cooperate is pure fantasy. And yet, these sealed batches of bottled Tenebrium in front of us look more like deliberately prepared "feed," meant to guide Devourborne into continuously replenishing the Nucleus's energy supply. How exactly was technology like this achieved? The answer completely escapes me...
—From the notes of Salfi

We have recovered many objects from Spatiotemporal Fragments that possessed both artistic and aesthetic value — some unsettling and mysterious, others sleek in their simplicity. But this one... I must admit, its sheer dullness borders on shocking. And yet, somehow, it also happens to be the only thing within this Spatiotemporal Fragment that could truly be called "art." Perhaps this iron plate and its circular patterns really do carry some profound meaning beyond comprehension, an attempt to reveal a kind of minimalist truth. But I lack the insight to prove it. For now, I'll leave the question unanswered and let future generations decide for themselves.
—Written by Art Critic Garcia

"You think parts like this are just lying around like trash?" He held the gear right up to your face. The teeth were still turning, while his own eyes looked cloudy and worn. "You think your pathetic little life could survive getting caught in those blades? You think when your body gets shredded over and over again, you won't be stuck paying a fortune in compensation fees? These scrap parts are worth way more than your life ever was!"
"They're the weapons. And you're just some expendable material."
Once a story is retold this way, what matters is no longer what truly happened, but the object left behind. Words shaped and polished become stories. Parts reshaped and reforged become weapons.

When you dug that chunk of coal out of the scrap pile, it was changing color. About the size of a fist, pitch black, no different from the thousands of other lumps scattered nearby. But the moment your mining lamp hit it, a faint blue-violet glow shimmered across its surface.
Not just the surface — the whole stone was glowing. That was when you realized it wasn't coal at all. At least, not the kind of coal you thought it was.
"What is that?" you asked, switching on your flashlight and letting a brighter beam fall over the coal.
"That's a battery. A living battery." Your squad leader answered calmly, as if she were talking about a rock that could breathe. She told you electricity had replaced fire, just as Attuners had replaced people like them.
"Pick it up. We'll need it on the road."
